observations: Baseline preserves actual 200000-byte streaming upload/status200/exact response size body before checking peer completion. A borrowed JoinHandle quiet wait retains handle; any returned JoinError or peer error propagates.
If old peer completes while client connection remains alive, the test explicitly fails. If quiet interval expires, it then drops client and awaits exact peer count under whole test timeout.
Fixed helper propagates release_capacity error immediately and drops incoming/response/respond handles before inline poll_closed, observing driver failure instead of spawning and discarding it.
Resolved poll_closed drives connection and stream state and completes on actual underlying closure. No extra detached shutdown task remains inside helper.
First early-final413 cancellation/reuse test is byte-preserved and still requires exact CANCEL plus real subsequent request.
Two other source files have only blank paragraph insertion after independent guards; no algorithm, condition, result or runtime behavior change.

bounds.scope: finite completion observation while live client; not a universal scheduler guarantee or leak-free runtime proof

ownership_limits: The test still starts its peer with a JoinHandle. Normal success joins it; errors/outer deadline can drop that handle without an explicit abort-and-join owner. The surrounding test runtime and dropped client/socket terminate scope, but this review does not claim all background failures are recovered on every exceptional path.
The corrected helper owns shutdown inline; this approval does not imply a full JoinSet conversion of the unchanged companion test.
readability: Changed streaming phases are separated: duplex/client setup, actual request and response, exact body assertion, finite quiet check, client drop and peer join. Body-capacity failure stays beside the consuming operation; explicit handle drops precede shutdown. Parser changes are two narrowly authorized paragraph boundaries.
